title: WaitForElementResult
description:
Outcome of a `wait_for_element`.

`satisfied` is the answer and `attached` / `visible` are the evidence: a timeout is **not** an RPC error, because "no, not within 10s — and here is what it looked like when I stopped looking" is a complete answer to the question that was asked. This mirrors `wait_for_navigation`'s `reached: "timeout"`.

The two booleans are reported separately rather than as one `observed` enum because presence and visibility are orthogonal, and **the reason for a timeout is the whole point of the report**: `attached: true, visible: false` says "it is there but hidden", `attached: false` says "it never appeared". A single enum cannot express both without losing one of them.

attached.description: Whether the target was still mounted in the DOM when the wait returned.

elapsed_ms.description: Wall-clock time spent waiting, including the final probe.

satisfied.description: Whether the requested state was reached before the deadline.

visible.description: Whether the target was visible when the wait returned. Always `false` when `attached` is `false`.

JavaScriptDialogHandledAction.description: How the extension resolved the dialog so CDP could continue.

JavaScriptDialogInfo.description: One observed + handled JavaScript dialog during a tool call.

sequence.description: Monotonic per-tab sequence for ordering within a session.

JavaScriptDialogType.description: Native JS dialog kind reported by CDP.
